Text:
California Democrat Ro Khanna has become the first member of Congress to sign the PEACE Pledge, a campaign finance and foreign policy commitment created by Track AIPAC. The pledge, short for Pledge to Enforce American Law, Counter Foreign Influence and End War Crimes, bars signatories from accepting campaign contributions, bundled donations, political support or outside spending from AIPAC, Democratic Majority for Israel, Republican Jewish Coalition, Christians United for Israel, their affiliated PACs or similar donor networks promoting unconditional support for Israel.

Track AIPAC, launched in 2024, monitors federal campaign spending by AIPAC and other pro-Israel groups using Federal Election Commission data. The group says the pledge is designed to cut the influence of pro-Israel lobbying money in US elections and force elected officials to follow US laws governing foreign aid, arms transfers and human rights. The pledge also commits signatories to reject funding routed through intermediary groups or coordinated donor activity.

The pledge includes support for First Amendment protections for Americans who criticize Israel, including supporters of boycott, divestment and sanctions campaigns. It also calls for opposition to military aid for any country whose forces commit war crimes, genocide, apartheid, ethnic cleansing or serious human rights violations. Khanna’s signature comes as Democratic divisions over Israel, Ga-za and US military assistance continue to deepen in Congress.

Text: There are fist fights among dentists who believe different things about TMD issues- lots of controversy! Here is my take after 54 years of dentistry (and lots of learning/unlearning!) 1.Most TMD symptoms are muscle symptoms- headache, neck ache, facial pain, popping jaws- you name it. Not the joint itself (even if the pain seems to be coming from there. 2.Many therapies that seem to help treat muscle overuse/pain. Botox, massage, PT, chiropractic, but too often, these are temporary solutions. 3. Unless the splint is carefully design and adjusted, all it is just plastic between the teeth. 4. A good diagnosis from a competent doctor, looking at the muscles, teeth AND how the teeth meet is imperitive! I advise finding someone who has a Tekscan so you and the dentist can see how the teeth are meeting and how that might be triggering jaw clenching or grinding….

Text:
I had a brutal dental procedure of having a crown prep for molar tooth #31 then a permanent crown was put in two weeks later.  

  The crown felt fine for two weeks after. Then just like that I got severe TMJ, horrible brain fog and severe vertigo. And my body felt inflamed. Could barely function. 

   I went back to the Dentist and the crown fits great, x-ray shows no infection and my bite alignment is good.  Dentist thinks it might be nerve related.  I just turned 70 so dental work seems to be harder on my system as well. Has anyone experienced anything similar?  I'm still having TMJ and vertigo issues.
